sections.overview: The Sandwich Tern is a coastal seabird breeding around the Atlantic and adjacent seas, then migrating widely after nesting.
sections.identification: It has a black shaggy crest and a long black bill tipped yellow, with a pale grey back and white underside. Unlike the Greater Crested Tern (T. bergii), its bill is not wholly yellow; see that profile.
sections.habitat: It nests colonially on low sandy or shingle coasts and islands, and feeds mainly in nearby shallow marine waters and estuaries.
sections.diet: It takes mostly small schooling fish by plunge-diving, and may also eat squid, shrimp and other small prey.
sections.behavior: It is a long-distance migrant and forms dense breeding colonies.
sections.reproduction: Pairs nest in a shallow ground scrape and usually lay one or two eggs, incubated by both parents.
sections.ecology: Its chiefly fish diet and nearshore feeding connect it to coastal shoals and estuarine food webs.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN category is Least Concern, though local colonies can be affected by disturbance, habitat change and reduced fish resources.
